name: Nebuzaradan
overview: Nebuzaradan was a male captain of the guard serving the King of Babylon, known for his role in overseeing the exile of captives. Scripture identifies him specifically in this military capacity, highlighting his involvement in the Babylonian conquest and deportation of the people of Judah. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded for him.
namesAndTitles: The name Nebuzaradan means 'Nebo [Nabu] has given seed [offspring],' reflecting a theophoric element referencing the Babylonian deity Nabu. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Kings 25:8, does not appear to have been given by God but rather reflects the cultural context of Babylon.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Nebuzaradan beyond his official role as captain of the guard. There are no known familial connections documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nebuzaradan plays a significant role in the biblical narrative as the Babylonian official charged with carrying out the exile of the people of Judah, an event that marked a pivotal moment in Israel's history. His actions under the authority of the Babylonian king contributed to the fulfillment of God's judgment on Judah for their unfaithfulness. Through his role, the narrative highlights the consequences of disobedience to God and sets the stage for future restoration.
